paragraphs.text: A small tuo of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yunnan, made in 1998. After the [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling), the leaf was steamed and pressed into a little dome with a hollow underneath. That places it in the style’s third decade: Yunnan’s state factories brought the pile into production in 1973, twenty-five years before this tea was made.
At twenty-eight years it is well past the ten that mark [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged) in the trade. How a tea like this has been kept shapes it as much as the years do.

brewing.text: From a cake, brick or tuo, ease a piece off along the edge with a pick rather than snapping it, so the leaves stay whole. Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
